topic: Biodiversity and the Need for Classification
title: Why Classify Living Things? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya takes one slow walk through the college garden and starts counting kinds of living things: a mango tree, grass, ants, a crow, moss, an earthworm, a butterfly on a hibiscus. Before she reaches the gate, she has lost count.

You will see what biodiversity really counts (the number and types of organisms, not individuals) and how many species are described so far (about 1.7 to 1.8 million). A zoom ladder goes from the mango tree to its bark, the soil below and one drop of soil water under a microscope. Then why we cannot study every kind one by one, what classification means, and a simple sorting key that runs live on the garden. A side by side comparison (grouping by use vs by features), a pause and think check, a worked example, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 4 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
